paragraphs.text: 1 “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, 2 I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land. 3 And they have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink. 4 “Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head; 5 Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things: 6 The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border. 7 Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head: 8 And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off: for the LORD hath spoken it.”

For repentance to be effective in the life of the Church and in the life of every member in it, we must look to the day of the Lord as being near. In it we see that the present disciplines, though bitter and sorrowful, are profitable for edification; we see the appearing of the Lord for our eternal salvation and the punishment of the wicked. Those who have fallen and are under discipline see that their glory is coming quickly and that the shame of the devil is truly being fulfilled. The prophet says: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land. And they have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink” [1-3].

The judgment takes place in the valley of Jehoshaphat, which in Hebrew means “the valley where Jehovah judges or condemns,” that is, “the valley of judgment”... This valley is not known with certainty, but the men of the fourth century held that it is the Kidron valley, east of Jerusalem, opposite the Mount of Olives to the west; some think it is the Valley of Walnuts north of Jerusalem, or the Valley of Rababa south of the city.
Why was the valley of Jehoshaphat chosen for the judgment?
First: It was chosen for its symbolic meaning, for Jehovah Himself is the One who judges; God is the Judge, because He searches the hearts and the reins.

Second: It is a valley near Jerusalem in which all are gathered, that God may judge the wicked according to their deeds and may bring His children into the heavenly Jerusalem, the glory of which the wicked are forbidden to see. The judgment is not held in Jerusalem, for nothing unclean or abominable enters it, but it is the dwelling of God with men (the saints) (Rev 21:3).

Third: The valley of Jehoshaphat reminds us of what happened with the armies of the nations that attacked Judah (2 Chr 20). The Lord shattered them in the very place where they had gathered to fight against His children, as though the criminal were being tried in the place of his crime. The Lord's promise to King Jehoshaphat and his people, who were crying out with humility and fasting, was: “Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God's... Set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD with you. And when Judah came toward the watch tower in the wilderness, they looked unto the multitude, and, behold, they were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped” (2 Chr 20:24). Truly, those who oppose us are a great multitude, and as the Apostle Paul says: “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places” (Eph 6:12). Yet we enjoy power against the devil and his hosts, the power of the Cross, which shatters their evil, “having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it” (Col 2:15). This is the valley of Jehoshaphat, where the Lord Christ, outside the camp, outside Jerusalem, destroyed the evil enemy by His Cross to bring us back to His eternal Kingdom! It is a judgment that was accomplished by the Cross, and its effectiveness remains in the life of everyone who is united with the Crucified One until he meets the Lord face to face on His great day. For this reason the Apostle Paul urges us: “Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come” (Heb 13:13-14). It is a call to go out to the valley of Jehoshaphat, outside Jerusalem, bearing the Cross of the Lord, so that we may see with our own eyes the defeat of the devil and his works being accomplished every day in our life, as we journey toward our abiding city.

Let us go forth to the valley of Jehoshaphat to see the Lord judging for us against the devil, his enticements and his threats. Let us grasp what the prophet declared beforehand: “For it is the day of the LORD's vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion” (Isa 34:8). “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come” (Isa 63:4). The day of vengeance has been accomplished and has truly come with the lifting up of the Lord on the Cross, drawing Zion to Himself from the midst of hell and crushing the powers of evil under His feet. This day remains extended in our life, as long as the sacrifice of the Cross has not been spoiled and hell has not prevailed over it; and when God's plan for all the elect is completed, the Lord appears to us face to face and the devil is seen bound in the abyss.
In this chapter God brought out His great day in its three aspects:

entries.section: 1. The judgment of the wicked in the valley of Jehoshaphat:

paragraphs.text: First: The glorification of the name of God, which the nations dishonored by attacking His children, for He says: “So shall ye know that I am the LORD your God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain” [17]. On the day of judgment God is glorified, who delivered His children from the captivity of the devil, declaring His eternal dwelling in their midst, as St. John says: “I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Rev 21:3).

Second: The humbling of the pride of the nations. As the prophet Isaiah says: “Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith? or shall the saw magnify itself against him that shaketh it? as if the rod should shake itself against them that lift it up, or as if the staff should lift up itself, as if it were no wood” (Isa 10:15). So the nations whom God used to discipline His people thought that they were greater than the One who permitted them to do so; they boasted against the true God and exalted themselves against Him. Therefore, after the purpose for which they were used is fulfilled, He returns and repays them for their deeds: “For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head” (Obad 1:15). For this reason the day of the Lord is called a day of destruction: “Howl ye; for the day of the LORD is at hand; it shall come as a destruction from the Almighty” (Isa 13:6). It is also called a day of vengeance: “For this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be satiate and made drunk with their blood” (Jer 46:10). “To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn” (Isa 16:2), “for the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come” (Isa 63:4). It is also called a day of wrath: “Before the fierce anger of the LORD come upon you, before the day of the LORD's anger come upon you” (Zeph 2:2).

Third: The complete deliverance of the people of God, who fell into bondage for a time and became a mockery to the nations. Therefore He says: “When I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem” [1]. He who permits us to be disciplined, even by bondage, since we accepted it by our own will, sends us help to set us free, as He sent Moses to Pharaoh, saying: “I say unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me” (Ex 4:23).

God looked and found His sons and daughters being sold through fornication and drunkenness: they sell the boy for a harlot and the girl for a cup of wine to drink! They sold them to the Javanites (the Greeks) [6], traders of souls (Ex 27:13). How hard it is indeed for the heart of God to see His inheritance, His own, His portion and His treasure, scattered by the tyrant enemy for the cheapest of prices! He is jealous over the souls of His sons and daughters, who are His treasure: His gold, His silver and His goodly pleasant things. Therefore He rises to set them free, saying to the enemy: “I will return your recompence, because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things: the children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Javanites, that ye might remove them far from their border... I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off: for the LORD hath spoken it” [4-8].

What are the silver, the gold and the goodly pleasant things that the enemy carries into his temples, if not the precious souls of the children of God, whom He counts in His sight as His precious treasure? The enemy has snatched them to work for the sake of a strange temple hostile to God, the temple of the love of the world and the enjoyment of the unclean pleasures of the flesh! The children of God were sold to strangers, and became slaves to many sins, like those under the power of Pharaoh and his men. But at all times the Lord affirms His saving work by the Cross for the sake of the souls of His servants, saying: “Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles' wings, and brought you unto myself. Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine: and ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation” (Ex 19:4-6). As it is said: “For the LORD's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance” (Deut 32:9). He works on behalf of His people, His portion, to set them completely free and make of them new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness (2 Pet 3:10-13). The enemy can no longer plunder it.

We have received from God His silver, which is His word... the living one, refined seven times (Ps 12:6), and His gold, that is, the heavenly mark, and He has given us the fruits of the Spirit, which are the goodly pleasant things. So we do not bring these into any temple other than the temple of the Lord, but we walk faithfully in what He has given us, that we may enjoy much more after having enjoyed repentance. They carried the goodly pleasant things of the Lord into their evil temples, like one who uses the marks of love that God gave him for the lusts of the flesh, or like one who exploits the love of others for him because of his religiosity or his spiritual knowledge in a way other than the way of the Lord!

Finally, what does the Lord mean by His saying: “I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans”? [8]. Perhaps He meant by this what happened in the days of the Maccabees, who overcame their enemies, or He means the judging of the world by the saints, as the Apostle says: “Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” (1 Cor 6:2). For when the wicked are deprived of glory they are judged through the saints, who gained eternal freedom through true repentance in the Lord.

entries.section: 2. The Lord is a refuge for His people:

paragraphs.text: 9 Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up: 10 Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong. 11 Assemble yourselves, and come, all ye heathen, and gather yourselves together round about: thither cause thy mighty ones to come down, O LORD. 12 “Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about. 13 Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great.” 14 Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of judgment: for the day of the LORD is near in the valley of judgment. 15 The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining. 16 The LORD also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but the LORD will be a refuge for his people, and a stronghold for the children of Israel. 17 “So shall ye know that I am the LORD your God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy, and there shall no strangers pass through her any more.

After declaring the great day of the Lord, in which God is glorified by delivering His children from the power of evil, He declared that the secret of victory is not in man himself but in God, his refuge.

He begins first by mocking the nations that relied on themselves and their own resources, to declare their weakness before God, who upholds His children and grants them victory. In derision He says: “Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up. Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong” [9-10].

They fight with all their strength, and behold, they shatter themselves, as it is said: “Associate yourselves, O ye people, and ye shall be broken in pieces... Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us” (Isa 8:9-10). Here too He asks them, if they wish, to prepare war, that is, to dedicate all their strength and resources to war, and to bring all their mighty men at once, to turn their plowshares (the teeth of the plow) into swords and their pruninghooks into spears, that is, to dedicate all their resources, for they are doomed to perish without fail!

entries.section: 2. The Lord is a refuge for His people:

paragraphs.text: In derision He says to them: “Let the weak say, I am strong” [10]. Satan thought himself a mighty man for a time of this measure, and did not realize that he is exceedingly weak when he enters the battle with the Lord Himself on the Cross.

Many of the Fathers see in the Lord's saying: “Let the weak say, I am strong” that these are words addressed to every believer who realizes that he is weak in himself, and who is strengthened in the Lord, his refuge, saying “I am strong.” As Abba Serenus says: [Hear what the King (God) Himself says, approving the brave men and summoning them to the spiritual war against sin, saying: “Let the weak say, I am strong, and the suffering say, I am a wrestler.” Only the weak fight in the Lord's battle... for “when I am weak, then am I strong” (2 Cor 12:9). And also: “for my strength is made perfect in weakness” (2 Cor 12:9)].

If we are weak before Satan, yet in the Lord we are strong and mighty men. As St. John Chrysostom wrote to his friend the fallen monk: [If Satan has this power to cast you down to the ground from the lofty height and exalted virtue to the farthest bounds of evil, how much more is He able to raise you up to your former confidence, and make you not only as you were, but happier than before]. [Satan made us fall and cast us down, but we must rise and not fall again, lest we cast ourselves down and add to his blows against us other blows].

entries.section: 2. The Lord is a refuge for His people:

paragraphs.text: Therefore let us not be terrified of the devil, even if he appears as many and mighty multitudes, for he is exceedingly weak before God who dwells in us. The prophet says: “Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of judgment: for the day of the LORD is near in the valley of judgment. The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining. The LORD also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but the LORD will be a refuge for his people, and a stronghold for the children of Israel” [14-16].
Even if the nations have become like the sun in the world, or the moon, or even the stars, yet before God, the Sun of Righteousness, they are darkened and their false brightness disappears.

The Lord Himself rises as a lion coming out of the tribe of Judah, protecting His children and fortifying them in Him. His voice thunders at sin, so that it trembles before Him and does not dwell in your soul (the heaven) or in your body (the earth).

St. Ephrem the Syrian speaks to us of God as a refuge for us, saying: [Let God be your refuge... If His providence does not forsake you, nothing can harm you. Do not fear the enemies who rush upon you violently, for God keeps your soul and turns harmful things into profitable things].

entries.section: 2. The Lord is a refuge for His people:

paragraphs.text: The sign of victory in the Lord is that, while we take refuge in Him as a stronghold for our souls, He reveals Himself in us and does not allow a stranger to reign in Jerusalem, His sanctuary, and no strangers pass through her any more [17].

18 “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the mountains shall drop down new wine, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the rivers of Judah shall flow with waters, and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the LORD, and shall water the valley of Shittim. 19 Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land. 20 But Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation. 21 For I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed: for the LORD dwelleth in Zion.”

Our victory in the Lord is declared by His dwelling alone in us, reigning over the heart and not allowing a stranger to pass through His kingdom... The earth and its fullness become the Lord's and His Christ's. This divine presence declares itself through the overflow of fruit that appears in us, and the springs of the Spirit that burst forth within us:

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the mountains shall drop down new wine (juice), and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the rivers of Judah shall flow with waters, and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the LORD, and shall water the valley of Shittim (acacia)” [18].

What are these mountains, hills, springs and the house of the Lord, if not aspects of the victorious Church in which the Lord, the Giver of victory, dwells, and makes of her children holy mountains for Him, flowing with juice that refreshes the mature, and living hills flowing with milk for the little ones, and unfailing springs to which all take refuge, and a house of the Lord that gladdens the heavenly ones?!

Perhaps He also points to the juice (the new wine) as the Holy Spirit, who makes the soul drunk with the love of God and fills it with eternal joy. The mountains point to those who labor in the Lord's vineyard. This divine Spirit is enjoyed by the mature as a gladdening spiritual wine, and the little ones feed on Him as milk that sustains them, and as living water that quenches every soul that thirsts for Him. The Lord Christ Himself says: “If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water” (Jn 7:37-38).

His speaking of the fountain that comes forth from the house of the Lord to water the valley of Shittim, or the valley of acacia, is the fountain of Baptism, which the prophet Ezekiel saw issuing from under the threshold of the house of the Lord toward the east, the waters coming down from under the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar, watering very many trees on this side and on that, its waters healing and containing very many fish (Ezek 47). It is the fountain of Baptism that overflows upon the dry and unfruitful valley of acacia, in which nothing grew but the acacia tree... Baptism turns it into a fertile valley, with every kind of fruitful tree! This is the river that overflowed with its four branches upon the nations in every part of the world, so that God might establish His living paradise instead of the barren valley of acacia (Shittim). This valley begins northwest of Jerusalem and descends to the east of the city, separating it from the Mount of Olives, then runs to the southeast toward the Dead Sea; perhaps it is today's Valley of Fire.

In any case, Joel concludes his prophecy by declaring the overflow of God's work in His Church, not only from the positive side, where she overflows with juice, milk and living waters, but also from the negative side, in which He shatters in her the works of the old man, who is symbolized here by Egypt (the love of the world), which enslaves man as Pharaoh enslaved the people of God, and by Edom (the love of bloodshed and injustice)... He prepares her for that great day, to be joined with Him in His eternal glory.
In this chapter the prophet Joel presents to us the following divine blessings:
a. The enemies are driven out and cast down to perish [1-15].
b. Jerusalem is saved [16, 17].
c. The land is blessed [18].
d. Judah is renewed [19-21].

This is the work of God in us, as He shatters the evil enemy under our feet, saves our inner Jerusalem, His holy temple, sanctifies our land, that is, our body, and declares the kingdom of the One who came out of the tribe of Judah in our depths.
Your day... is the day of freedom!
* You permitted Your people to be disciplined, by their captivity in Babylon, but soon You disciplined violent and cruel Babylon.
You made Your day a day of freedom and joy!
* Judge, O Lord, my sin that has held me captive in humiliation, but my soul, beloved to You, set free with Your right hand!
* I confess to You that I have corrupted Your gifts to me; I have turned my energies and my emotions and all my resources to evil.
Sanctify my life, renew my depths, return all my energies to Your Kingdom!
* I confess to You that I am a prisoner of sin...
I am weak, and despised!
But in You I become strong!
By Your Cross I shatter the chains of the enemy and my soul is set free.
The day of Your crucifixion is the day of the declaration of my freedom!
